synthesis: The resolvent trace is the common carrier, but its mathematical status changes with the available geometry. For Euclidean and hyperbolic quotients, a free Green kernel can be summed over discrete-group images; quotient identifications and then conjugacy classes turn group elements into primitive lengths and repetitions, producing exact smoothed rectangle and Selberg trace identities. For a generic Hamiltonian without that image construction, the long-path Green kernel is only semiclassical, and tracing it plus stationary phase selects periodic orbits and yields the asymptotic Gutzwiller formula.
source_support: Unit v2u03 proves the periodic rectangle image sum is an exact boundary-compatible Green function and recovers its trace formula; v2u04 identifies discrete quotient geometry and invariant hyperbolic data as the transfer conditions; v2u07 evaluates hyperbolic conjugacy classes and assembles the smoothed Selberg identity; v2u13 instead obtains the generic orbit sum from a semiclassical Green function by saddle selection and monodromy weighting.
nonparaphrase_operation: Compares two derivations through the same resolvent representation and isolates discrete quotient structure as the extra dependency that upgrades a trajectory expansion from semiclassical stationary phase to an exact group-image trace identity.
limits: The rectangle orbit sum is not convergent without a decaying test function; the displayed Selberg formula assumes an even analytic decaying test function and only hyperbolic nonidentity elements. Gutzwiller assumes the semiclassical limit and isolated unstable periodic orbits and does not resolve convergence or stable/continuous orbit families. Exact kernels, transformations, constants, phases, and determinant normalizations remain scan-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted because v2u03/v2u04/v2u07 jointly establish the quotient-image mechanism while v2u13 supplies a materially different generic construction, so the exact-versus-asymptotic distinction and its controlling dependency are unavailable from either side alone.

synthesis: The diagonal approximation first turns smoothing into equal-action pairing, but its unavoidable large-time plateau contradiction shows that unequal labels must remain coherently correlated. In the Riemann case, rewriting prime powers with the von Mangoldt function makes the missing object a shifted mean of Lambda(n)Lambda(n+r); assuming Hardy-Littlewood then converts rational arithmetic data into the oscillatory GUE term. For the modular surface, normalizing conjugacy multiplicities similarly exposes a shifted correlation gamma(r), and finite residue-class means feed a rational-pole generating-function reconstruction of the form factor.
source_support: Unit v2u18 derives the short-time diagonal slope and independently proves equal-action-only growth cannot give the large-time plateau. Unit v2u20 changes prime/repetition indexing to Lambda weights and isolates the near-diagonal shifted mean. Unit v2u23 conditionally inserts the Hardy-Littlewood series, localizes on coprime rational data, and recovers the missing oscillatory GUE term. Unit v2u29 repeats the shifted-correlation reduction for normalized modular multiplicities and uses finite modular residue means and rational boundary poles to construct their Fourier data and hence R2 and K.
nonparaphrase_operation: Links an internally falsified approximation to two source-specific repairs, showing that a change from individual classical labels to shifted arithmetic correlations is the shared missing representation and that rational residue/pole data are the proposed completion device in both settings.
limits: The Riemann calculation assumes Hardy-Littlewood, smoothing, small shifts, localization, and a continuum replacement. The modular calculation assumes gamma exists, replaces products by their mean, invokes the finite-modular theorem from [23], and uses continuum, Tauberian, rational-pole dominance, and extended-neighborhood approximations. It is therefore not a generic or unconditional proof of off-diagonal statistics; several correction factors and Fourier conventions are scan-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted because v2u18 establishes the obstruction, while v2u20/v2u23 and v2u29 independently realize the same shifted-correlation dependency in prime-power and modular-orbit representations, with the conjectural and heuristic proof burdens preserved.

synthesis: Arithmeticity constrains traces across field embeddings, so the number of available trace values grows like the square root of the total orbit count; via the trace-length map this creates exponentially large exact length families. Their coherent multiplicity gain, inserted into the diagonal form factor, can reach order one near the Ehrenfest scale even though the underlying hyperbolic motion remains classically chaotic. The critical exponent is one half: non-arithmetic controls with subcritical exponential multiplicity need not depart from GOE. Hecke correspondences provide a separate commuting-operator picture of the same arithmetic exceptionalism, but the source does not derive Poisson statistics from that symmetry algebra.
source_support: Unit v2u25 combines integer-trace compression with total orbit growth and reports Poisson-like spectra despite classical chaos. Unit v2u27 generalizes the compression using bounded nonidentity embeddings and a lattice-volume trace count. Unit v2u28 propagates the resulting multiplicity through orbit density and amplitude into an exponentially growing diagonal form factor. Unit v2u33 derives the lambda=1/2 threshold and supplies subcritical non-arithmetic GOE controls. Unit v2u31 constructs automorphy-preserving commuting Hecke operators while explicitly denying a precise implication to Poisson statistics.
nonparaphrase_operation: Composes embedding-bounded trace counting with the trace-length map and the spectral form-factor weights, then uses non-arithmetic exponent controls to identify the rate rather than mere degeneracy as the operative discriminator; it also separates this causal chain from the Hecke symmetry analogy.
limits: The arithmetic diagonal calculation is asymptotic, dominated by long primitive orbits, and its post-crossover plateau is an explicit interpolation rather than an off-diagonal derivation. Finite non-arithmetic multiplicity fits have no accuracy or asymptotic guarantee, and the threshold only removes a diagonal contradiction rather than proving GOE. Hecke commutativity is not proved to cause Poisson statistics, and its eigenfunction discussion uses numerical nondegeneracy plus Fourier normalization assumptions. Quantitative constants, fits, matrices, amplitudes, and conventions are scan-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted because v2u25/v2u27/v2u28 form a concrete arithmetic-trace-to-orbit-family-to-spectrum mechanism, v2u33 supplies a discriminating counter-control, and v2u31 is retained only at its supported status as a parallel structural explanation rather than an unsupported causal theorem.
